_comment: vibekit's BUNDLED TOOLS: the tools this product ships with because it
needs them, plus the ones it recommends for a good experience.
These are not a layer over the tool catalog. The catalog is a
REFERENCE -- every tool the mise and aqua registries can express,
translated, with no opinion about which ones matter -- and this file
is the bundle vibekit is shipping out of it. Each entry declares which
of the two it is:
essential: true   NECESSARY. A vibekit feature stops working without
it (gh/glab/tea back the Sources tab, node runs
npx-based MCP servers, uv runs the Python ones).
The engine refuses to delete the row and the UI
offers no delete control. Disabling is still
allowed, which is the escape hatch.
featured: true    RECOMMENDED. Surfaced first in the Add-tool modal
as the starter set, and removable like anything
else.
The engine applies this to EVERY catalog it loads (baked, cached,
fetched), so a bundled tool survives a catalog refresh, and
`toolcatalog verify -overlay` gates the same set at image build.
An entry with no source names a tool the registries already carry and
adds only what vibekit knows about it: whether it is necessary or
recommended, and the copy the UI shows. An entry WITH a source is a
tool no registry carries, so the bundle has to define it outright.
A bare "aqua:owner/repo" source is the one thing that cannot appear
here: resolving it needs an aqua-registry checkout, which exists at
catalog COMPILE time and not at runtime. Everything here is either
sourceless, a release: source (whose version is resolved from the
forge on every update) or a manual: install script.
upstream: {...} is read by cplieger/.github's Renovate customManager
to bump a hand-pinned version. Only a manual entry needs one -- a
release: entry resolves its own latest tag, which is why glab, clangd
and kotlin-language-server carry no pin at all.
Manual install commands run under bash with VERSION, VERSION_NOPFX
(leading v stripped), BIN, TOOLS, OPT and the ARCH_*_OR_* variables in
the environment (value = left side on amd64, right side on arm64).

node.description: Node.js runtime. Required for npx-based MCP servers and npm-installed language servers.

go.description: Go toolchain. Required for go-installed tools and full gopls analysis.

uv.description: Python package runner (uv). Provides uvx for Python MCP servers and installs pip-sourced tools.

github-cli.description: GitHub CLI. Installed automatically when you connect a GitHub account in Sources.

glab.description: GitLab CLI. Installed automatically when you connect a GitLab account in Sources.

tea.description: Gitea/Codeberg CLI. Installed automatically when you connect a Gitea account in Sources.

clangd.description: C/C++ LSP (~160 MB). Reads compile_commands.json from your workspace. Upstream ships x86_64 builds only — not available on arm64 hosts.

rust.description: Rust toolchain (rustup + rustc + cargo, minimal profile). Required for cargo-installed tools and full rust-analyzer analysis.
rust.install: curl -fsSL https://sh.rustup.rs | RUSTUP_HOME="${OPT}/rustup" CARGO_HOME="${OPT}/cargo" sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable --profile minimal --no-modify-path && for b in cargo rustc rustup; do ln -sf "${OPT}/cargo/bin/$b" "${BIN}/$b"; done

java.description: OpenJDK 21 JRE (Eclipse Temurin). Required by jdtls and kotlin-language-server; shared between them.
java.install: safe_tag=$(printf '%s' "${VERSION}" | sed 's/+/%2B/g') && rel=$(printf '%s' "${VERSION}" | sed 's/jdk-//;s/+/_/') && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/adoptium/temurin21-binaries/releases/download/${safe_tag}/OpenJDK21U-jre_${ARCH_X86_64_OR_AARCH64}_linux_hotspot_${rel}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "${OPT}" --strip-components=1 && ln -sf "${OPT}/bin/java" "${BIN}/java" && ln -sf "${OPT}/bin/keytool" "${BIN}/keytool"

jdtls.description: Java LSP (Eclipse JDT language server). Requires the java runtime.

kotlin-language-server.description: Kotlin LSP. Requires the java runtime (shared with jdtls).
